correctness.rationale: For arbitrary integers m,n>=2 and positive alpha,beta,gamma, the four tensor-product eigenspace projectors of H0 have positive sink weights and only UV/VU can collide, at m alpha=n beta. The rank-one contraction lemma identifies the exact bright cyclic space; the Cauchy identity gives the sitewise capture deficit and 4-versus-3 bright-rank mean. An explicit bright-complement rank-one resolvent at the middle collision and analytic simple-eigenvalue perturbation give the imaginary quadratic coefficient 4mn(m-1)(n-1)/(gamma(m+n-2)^3). Orthogonal dark/bright dynamics and spectral gap yield the double-time-scale survival. Rebuilt exact full-matrix projector tests passed 170 cases, complex eigenvalue linewidth tests 24 cases, and exponentiated full-matrix survival tests 32 cases. Finite experiments corroborate and do not prove all-size statements. Exact scope, positivity and fixed-parameter limits are stated in RESULT.md.

value.rationale: The vertex-resolved capture discontinuity at a tunable anisotropy collision and universal one-quarter change in average single-sink efficiency characterize a natural coherent transport threshold for every complete-graph Cartesian product. An exact positive detuning-squared decay coefficient and full fixed-size long-time survival law quantify how formerly dark mass leaks on the metastable scale. These sharpen the qualitative dark-subspace mechanism, distinguishing sources with versus without critical-mode overlap and yielding falsifiable finite-size predictions; this is not a mere calculation of a single arbitrary matrix. The general Krylov-space projection formula by itself is acknowledged prior mathematics, so the value assessment rests on sharp evaluated resonance coefficients and singular transport behavior.
